back: Work done per unit positive charge by an external agency in bringing it from infinity to a point. V = W/q.
V = Q/(4*pi*epsilon_0*r). Scalar, falls as 1/r.
V = (1/4*pi*epsilon_0)(p*cos(theta)/r^2). Falls as 1/r^2, depends on angle.
V = +p/(4*pi*epsilon_0*r^2) at theta=0; V = -p/(4*pi*epsilon_0*r^2) at theta=pi.
V = 0. Potentials from +q and -q cancel exactly.
E = -dV/dl. Field points in direction of steepest potential decrease. Magnitude = rate of change of V per unit distance normal to equipotential.
U = (1/4*pi*epsilon_0)(q1*q2/r12). Positive for like charges (repulsive), negative for unlike (attractive).

front: Potential energy of dipole in uniform field
back: U = -pE*cos(theta). Minimum when aligned (theta=0), maximum when anti-aligned (theta=pi).

front: Work to assemble a system of 3 charges

back: (1) E=0 inside. (2) E normal to surface. (3) No excess charge inside. (4) V constant throughout. (5) E_surface = sigma/epsilon_0. (6) Cavity shielded.

front: E at surface of charged conductor
back: E = (sigma/epsilon_0) * n_hat. Derived using pillbox Gaussian surface.
E = 0 inside any charge-free cavity of a conductor, regardless of cavity shape or external fields. Used to protect instruments.
C = Q/V. Depends only on geometry and dielectric. Unit: Farad (1 F = 1 C/V).
C_0 = epsilon_0*A/d.
C = K*C_0 = K*epsilon_0*A/d. Capacitance increases by factor K.
K = epsilon/epsilon_0 > 1. Ratio of capacitance with dielectric to capacitance with vacuum.
1/C = 1/C_1 + 1/C_2 + ... Equivalent capacitance < smallest individual.
C = C_1 + C_2 + ... Equivalent capacitance > largest individual.
u = (1/2)*epsilon_0*E^2. Energy per unit volume. General result for any charge configuration.
P = epsilon_0*chi_e*E. Dipole moment per unit volume. chi_e = electric susceptibility.
1 eV = 1.6 x 10^-19 J. Kinetic energy gained by electron through 1 V potential difference.
V = q/(4*pi*epsilon_0*r) for r >= R. Same as point charge at centre.
V = q/(4*pi*epsilon_0*R). Constant everywhere inside (since E = 0 inside).
